explanation: Sodium hydrogencarbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid the same way sodium carbonate does, releasing carbon dioxide — the second of NCERT's two paired test tubes demonstrating this general pattern.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: Colourless dilute hydrochloric acid, with white sodium hydrogencarbonate added.
beaker_view.observation: Just like sodium carbonate, the hydrogencarbonate fizzes briskly with the acid, giving off carbon dioxide gas.
